Genetic status across the conservation-genomics toolkit: GBF indicators, contemporary N_e, and genetic load — and how fragile each verdict is to analyst choices

Author

andakprapakorn

Published

July 18, 2026

1 Introduction

Two chapters exercise the modern conservation-genomics toolkit on public whole-genome data: (1) the new Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) genetic-diversity indicators applied to the endangered green peafowl (Pavo muticus), and (2) realized-versus-masked genetic load in the inbred Scandinavian wolf (Canis lupus). The cross-cutting question is not “what is the number?” but “how fragile is the verdict to defensible analyst choices?” — filtering stringency, whether population structure is modelled, the GERP threshold that defines a deleterious site, and the run-of-homozygosity length that counts as inbreeding. Where a headline moves under choices a competent analyst could each justify, we report the movement itself as the result.

The GBF adopted a genetic-diversity target — the proportion of populations with effective size \(N_e > 500\) (Hoban et al. 2020; Mastretta-Yanes et al. 2024) — that is now being operationalized by national reporters. A central practical question is how stable that indicator is when computed from real, small-sample data. The wolf chapter provides a contrasting, data-rich case where the source study (Smeds et al. 2023) published a per-individual load table we can reproduce exactly, letting us separate genuine signal from analyst sensitivity.

2 Methods

2.1 Data

  • Green peafowl — Dong et al. (2021), Dryad 10.5061/dryad.ffbg79ctc. Modern resequencing across three regional populations plus six museum specimens. After a kinship screen (below) the analysis set is 22 unrelated individuals across Yunnan (n = 7), Vietnam (n = 10), Thailand (n = 5); Cambodia (n = 1) is dropped. A separate museum-versus-modern comparative callset supports the temporal-erosion angle (5 museum and 6 modern individuals after comparative-sample QC).
  • Scandinavian wolf — Smeds et al. (2023), Dryad 10.5061/dryad.7m0cfxpzj. 211 individuals with ancestral-allele-polarized SNPs (INFO/AA, two outgroups), VEP/SIFT coding annotation, and per-site GERP conservation scores. Individuals carry a time-period label (founding cohort ~1983 through 2007–2014) plus outbred references (Finland, Russia, immigrants).

All analyses start from the deposited VCFs (no re-calling from reads); every threshold lives in config/config.yaml, and the fragility axes are that config made executable.

2.2 QC and filtering (peafowl)

Two callsets are derived from a shared normalized parent (bcftools norm -m -any, biallelic SNPs on the 32 autosomes): unpruned Set A (neutral) feeds currentNe2, while an LD-pruned derivative of Set A feeds the structure analyses; Set B (lightly filtered, no MAF/MAC/HWE/LD-prune) feeds diversity and preserves rare alleles. The filtering-stringency knob re-derives Set A per preset — lenient / standard / strict (max-missing 0.7/0.8/0.9, min-GQ 15/20/30, min-DP 4/6/8, MAC 3) — yielding 1,046,916 / 420,826 / 30,143 post-MAC sites (a ~35× spread). Per-population HWE (\(P < 10^{-6}\) in any population) is applied to avoid Wahlund false departures. A confirmatory KING kinship screen retains all 22 individuals.

2.3 Contemporary \(N_e\) and the fragility cube (peafowl)

The parameter sweep is {filter} × {structure} → results/cube/results_cube.parquet, with currentNe2 as the sole automated estimator. LD-based \(N_e\) estimators read \(N_e\) out of linkage disequilibrium, so the un-pruned Set A is fed with a genome size of 32 Morgans (the autosome count), invoking currentNe2’s cross-chromosome (“no genetic map needed”) mode (Santiago et al. 2024); LD-pruning would destroy the very signal being measured. The structure knob contrasts modelled (per_population, the three values feeding the GBF fraction) with ignored (pooled, all 22 lumped — a Wahlund-biased cautionary contrast). NeEstimator-LDNe is a manual field-standard cross-check outside the DAG; GONE2 provides a recent-trajectory context panel only (a borrowed avian recombination rate, macrochromosomes only), never the contemporary indicator (Waples 2024).

2.4 GBF indicators (peafowl)

From the cube we compute the \(N_e > 500\) indicator (proportion of per-population estimates above threshold, per preset) and a robustness table (verdict stability across presets). The complementary Populations Maintained (PM) indicator is non-genomic, curated from IUCN/BirdLife range records at country resolution; a census \(N_c\) proxy contrast uses a conservative vertebrate \(N_e{:}N_c = 0.1\) (Frankham 1995). The three-state verdict — pass / fail / indeterminate (CI straddles 500, or no convergence) — is precomputed in the workflow.

2.5 Genetic load and ROH (wolf)

Per-individual load faithfully re-implements Smeds et al. (2023)’s gerp_load_polarized.py. For each SNP the derived allele is the non-ancestral allele (INFO/AA); a site is deleterious at threshold \(t\) if its GERP RS score \(> t\). Per individual we accumulate, in a single per-chromosome VCF stream, GERP-weighted realized load (\(\sum 2g\) over homozygous-derived deleterious sites \(/\) calls) and masked load (\(\sum g\) over heterozygous deleterious sites \(/\) calls), summing raw counts across chromosomes. We extend the source method by sweeping the GERP threshold over {2, 3, 4} in one pass — the wolf-side fragility knob — while GERP > 4 reproduces the deposit’s precomputed table exactly (Results). Runs of homozygosity are called with bcftools roh (GT-based HMM, a documented constant recombination rate) and summarized as per-individual \(F_{ROH}\) swept over a ROH-length cutoff, with long ROH (\(\geq 1.5\) Mb) read as recent inbreeding (Bertorelle et al. 2022).

3 Results

3.1 Peafowl: diversity, structure, and temporal contrast

PCA cleanly separates the three populations (minimum centroid gap 91.3 versus maximum within-population spread 38.3), though per-axis variance is low (PC1 ≈ 9.1%) and ADMIXTURE cross-validation favours \(K\) = 1 — a small-\(n\) artefact, so structure is read from PCA rather than a “best \(K\)”. Thailand is least diverse (expected heterozygosity 0.395; rarefied allelic richness 1.93), and Yunnan shows a heterozygote deficit (\(F_{IS}\) = 0.086) consistent with elevated within-population relatedness. The museum-versus-modern temporal contrast (angle G) is weak and metric-dependent: median \(\pi\) and \(H_o\) are marginally higher in museum specimens (erosion-consistent), but \(H_e\) and rarefied allelic richness are essentially flat. We report a direction, not an erosion claim, with aDNA-deamination and geographic-mismatch caveats.

3.2 Peafowl: contemporary \(N_e\) and the fragility of the GBF verdict

No population confidently passes \(N_e > 500\) under any filtering preset (0/3 / 0/3 / 0/3 pass for lenient / standard / strict). Verdicts are fail (point and 90% CI below 500) or indeterminate. Under the lenient preset the cross-chromosome estimates are Yunnan 55 [20–152], Thailand 76 [18–320], and Vietnam 2,293 [139–37,795] — the lone point above 500, but with a CI straddling it, hence indeterminate, not a pass. Under stricter presets several per-population estimates fail to converge (extreme heterozygote excess at small \(n\)), so convergence itself is preset-fragile (Table: results/tables/gbf_robustness.tsv). Pooling across populations (structure ignored) trends low and rises with stringency (52 → 89 → 108), below most per-population estimates — the predicted Wahlund direction, muddied by small-\(n\) noise.

The result is therefore two-sided: the headline is robust (0/3 pass regardless of preset), while the underlying estimates are fragile (2/3 populations change verdict across presets; Vietnam is estimable under lenient but not under stricter filters). The GONE2 context trajectory shows a recent decline (approximately 3,577 → 176 over ~416 generations), consistent with an endangered species but presented as context only.

3.3 Peafowl: the two GBF indicators disagree

The genomic indicator gives 0/3 populations \(N_e\)-secure, whereas Populations Maintained = 0.70 (7/10 range units maintained; no unresolved swing cases). All three sampled populations lie within the “maintained” set — yet none is genetically secure. Range-wide census (~10,000–19,999 mature, EN) nominally clears the \(N_c \geq 5\,000\) proxy, but that is the wrong denominator for a per-population indicator: the species is fragmented into subpopulations far below it (e.g. Keo Seima ~745). Still present ≠ genetically viable — the gap between the two Goal-A indicators is the communicable point, and a caution for reporters who might read occupancy-based indicators as sufficient.

3.4 Wolf: exact reproduction, then the fragility axes

At GERP > 4 the per-individual realized and masked loads reproduce the deposit’s precomputed LoadPerInd.thres4 table exactly — 95th-percentile relative error 1.3e-14 and raw count deltas of 0/0/0 across all 211 individuals — confirming the re-implementation is faithful before any extension. The biological signal is recovered correctly: the inbred Scandinavian cohorts carry realized > masked load (0.091–0.105 realized versus 0.052–0.079 masked), whereas outbred references (Finland, Russia, immigrants) carry masked > realized (0.100–0.101 masked versus 0.085–0.089 realized) — the masked-to-realized conversion expected when inbreeding exposes recessive load (Smeds et al. 2023; Bertorelle et al. 2022).

Both knobs move magnitude but not the pattern. Mean realized load falls 0.172 → 0.136 → 0.093 across GERP 2/3/4 (a stricter conservation filter keeps fewer, higher-confidence sites), and mean \(F_{ROH}\) falls 0.226 → 0.167 as the ROH-length cutoff rises 0.1 → 2 Mb (separating recent long ROH from ancient background). The realized-versus-masked direction is robust to the GERP threshold — the wolf-side counterpart to the peafowl fragility finding: the number depends on the choice, the signal does not.

4 Limitations

We claim risk, not demonstrated inbreeding depression. For the peafowl, small per-population \(n\) (7/10/5) yields wide \(N_e\) CIs and many indeterminate verdicts by construction; the estimates should not be cited as point values, and the temporal contrast is geographically narrow and aDNA-sensitive. Both chapters are reanalyses of published data, so the peafowl conclusion (“small, fragmented populations have small \(N_e\)”) is expected rather than novel, and the wolf load reproduces a published result. The genuine contribution is methodological: a quantified demonstration that a live policy indicator (the GBF \(N_e > 500\) verdict) and a load estimate are sensitive to defensible analyst choices, with the two GBF indicators shown to disagree on the same species. GONE2 (borrowed rate) and the ROH recombination rate (no dense wolf map) are documented approximations. The fragility cube quantifies, rather than hides, this uncertainty.

5 What evidence would change the conclusion?

The limitations above are decision points, not promises to collect more data. This evidence map identifies the smallest defensible next observation for each unresolved inference; none is required to reproduce the present analysis.

Current conclusion What remains unresolved Most useful next evidence How it would change the decision
No sampled peafowl population confidently clears \(N_e>500\). Wide confidence intervals and non-convergence at population sample sizes 7/10/5. More independently sampled individuals per population. Narrower intervals could turn an indeterminate cell into pass or fail; until then, retain the three-state verdict.
The GONE2 trajectory is consistent with recent decline but is context only. Peafowl linkage distances are approximated with a borrowed avian recombination rate. A species-specific recombination map. It would test the trajectory’s timing and scale; it would not replace currentNe2 as the contemporary GBF input.
Genomic patterns indicate inbreeding risk, not demonstrated inbreeding depression. The project has no direct measure of survival, fertility, or reproductive success. Individual fitness and reproductive measurements linked to genomic inbreeding. A genotype–fitness association could support a depression claim; load and ROH alone cannot.
Populations Maintained is 0.70 (7/10 range units maintained; no unresolved swing cases) at country resolution. Country-level presence can hide sub-country loss and fragmentation. Verified, time-stamped sub-country occurrence or occupancy records. Finer records would revise the PM denominator/numerator and show whether nominally extant units retain multiple populations.
Adding loci alone is unlikely to resolve the peafowl uncertainty. Millions of SNPs do not create more independent genomes; LD-based uncertainty is dominated by very small individual samples. Prioritize additional individuals before additional SNP density. If uncertainty shrinks with more individuals, sampling—not marker count—was limiting; otherwise estimator/model choice needs renewed scrutiny.

6 Reproducibility statement

All analytical results are built by the Snakemake DAG from two public deposits; the Streamlit explorer reads the outputs only.

The report performs a render-time schema check and reads its headline analytical values from the following workflow outputs. Missing files or columns stop the render rather than preserving stale prose.

CONDA_SUBDIR=osx-64 micromamba create -n congen -f environment.lock.yml  # Apple Silicon/Rosetta
micromamba activate congen && conda config --env --set subdir osx-64
scripts/build_tools.sh                                 # currentNe2 + GONE2, pinned commits
scripts/fetch_data.sh && scripts/extract_data.sh       # Dryad data
snakemake --cores 4                                    # phases 1-4: cube + GBF tables + wolf load/ROH
report/render_report.sh                                # schema-check values and render report/report.html
streamlit run app/streamlit_app.py                     # the live fragility explorer

Every threshold and parameter lives in config/config.yaml; per-phase gates (validate_phase{1..4}) assert the outputs are well-formed and, for the wolf load, reconcile against the deposit’s own numbers. R packages ship with the conda environment (R is conda-owned; no renv.lock).
